# E01 fixture provenance

All fixtures are local, mandatory inputs to `cargo test`. Tests never skip a
missing corpus and do not download files at runtime.

## dfVFS fixtures

`ext2.E01`, `ext2.split.E01`, `ext2.split.E02`, and the decoded contents of
`ext2.raw.gz` come from [log2timeline/dfvfs](https://github.com/log2timeline/dfvfs/tree/d365f334da42169276e2083a27f75bc2afa48ea8/test_data)
at commit `d365f334da42169276e2083a27f75bc2afa48ea8`. The E01 files are unchanged.
`ext2.raw.gz` is the upstream `ext2.raw` wrapped in gzip with `mtime=0` to save
space; its decoded bytes are unchanged. The upstream Apache 2.0 license is
included as `LICENSE.dfvfs`. Copyright belongs to the dfVFS project contributors.

Both E01 sets describe the same 4,194,304-byte disk. `ext2.E01` is compressed;
the two-file set is uncompressed and splits after chunk 95.

| Upstream file | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| ext2.E01 | ab9ea9a4951b74c37025ba40a978e85b1e4a0d94438080afb636144170d3f35b |
| ext2.split.E01 | d14f130c462b0ab8efb6bb44bbfe5680e00ffaa90538cde84579d1eb0dcac00f |
| ext2.split.E02 | b508375954ec1d1caeed8a6e5fc503f98493816ad6a3af89f5d220244c5f2864 |
| ext2.raw (before gzip) | a6c2f0e39afe6c6ab432ca5465349fcefe8dc944398e97b2d957d3f89dbb5d80 |

Decoded media MD5: `196066add11fb71c4c49cf1bb50d6d24`.
Decoded media SHA1: `4766c63c7acd5175015e3e8b90013a827e63f4ee`.

Refresh with `python tools/fetch_fixtures.py`. Downloads are pinned to the
commit and their SHA256 values are checked before writing.

## libewf-generated fixtures

`libewf-encase{1..6}-c{0,2}.E01` and `libewf-ftk-c{0,2}.E01` were produced
by the **libewf 20130416 C writer**, using `tools/validate_libewf.py --generate`.
They were not generated by the Rust parser or its test builders. These labels
refer to libewf's writer profiles, not to testing against the commercial tools.
There is no confirmed EnCase 7 writer fixture in this corpus; this old library
accepted format value 7 but emitted a minimal generic layout, so those files
were excluded.

The source media is deterministic mixed incompressible, zero, and repeated-byte
data, with 512-byte sectors, 64 sectors per chunk, four full chunks, and a
512-byte final chunk. Its original bytes are preserved in `libewf.raw.gz`.
EnCase 1 exercises inline tables; later variants exercise sectors/table/table2.
EnCase 6 fixtures include SHA1 as well as MD5. Fixtures contain writer-generated
acquisition timestamps, so a new generation may change container hashes.

Decoded raw size: 131,584 bytes.
Decoded raw SHA256: `dc35a1daa9c8111ebfdbc145c53165fdf171b0ebe78b13fd34112addb3c1edc0`.
Decoded raw MD5: `1cccd033947fea762cc4b98b4e48b744`.
Decoded raw SHA1: `d79762d0d99d8f7dd127957de25a595faa70ffeb`.

To regenerate, move the existing `libewf-*.E01` fixtures out of this directory
and run the command below. The generator refuses to overwrite containers.

```powershell
python tools/validate_libewf.py --library "D:\Projects\autopsy\thirdparty\ewfexport_exec\64-bit\libewf.dll" --generate
```

The ordinary Rust tests compare every decoded byte with the raw source data.
The optional validation script separately reads every fixture through libewf,
exports it through the Rust CLI, and compares both results with the source raw
data. Fixture checksums are recorded in `SHA256SUMS` for the committed corpus.
